title: Add interleaved span sampler and log-compact index for long-running streams
author: Asha Kumar
release_notes: Introduces an interleaved span sampler (cost-aware, token-phase aware) and a log-compact indexing path for long-running streaming invocations. Reduces observability storage footprint and improves SLO signal-to-noise for tail latency/cost alerts. Backwards compatible; default rollout is canary.
description:
Motivation: Long-running streaming invocations and high-cardinality client patterns are flooding trace/log backends with low-value spans and repeated log noise. This creates storage pressure, slows query amplification, and increases alert churn for token-level cost/latency SLOs.

What this PR does: Adds a lightweight interleaved span sampler in the runtime trace exporter that alternates between (1) dense sampling for the early phases of an invocation, and (2) cost-weighted sparse sampling for the long tail. The sampler is token-phase aware (prefix, generation, finalize) so we preserve fidelity on high-impact phases while aggressively compacting long-running steady-state spans. In parallel we add a log-compact indexing pipeline that deduplicates repetitive log sequences and emits a compact, queryable index that links to representative full samples on demand.

Included changes (single-string summary):
- Runtime: trace/sampler/interleaved_sampler.go (implements phase-aware sampling with pluggable policy)
- Exporter: trace/exporter/compact_indexer.go (streaming dedupe + index shard format)
- Telemetry: metrics/metrics_registry.go (new metrics: obs.span_sample_rate, obs.compact_index_hits, obs.compact_index_miss)
- Dashboards: grafana/streaming-compact-index.json and grafana/span-sampler-overview.json
- Alerts: alerting/streaming-alerts.yaml (updates to token-tail SLO alert to use compact-index-derived baselines)
- Tests: unit + integration harness for sampler and indexer, simulating 10k long-running streamed invocations

Commit summary:
- 1f3a2be: initial interleaved sampler implementation + unit tests
- 2c9d4ff: compact index format and exporter integration
- 4b7e1aa: metrics + dashboard panels
- 7c8f9d3: alert tuning and canary rollout flags
- bd0a8f1: integration tests and benchmark harness results

Key metrics observed in local bench (canary cohort):
- 62% reduction in trace storage for streams > 30s
- 48% reduction in observability query CPU for streaming-heavy queries
- No measurable increased token billing variance in canary (95th percentile token-cost deviation < 0.5%)

Rollout and safety:
- Default policy is OFF for existing customers; rollout controlled via feature_flag.observability.interleaved_sampler and via per-tenant config in Dedicated/Private.
- Canary run: 5% of requests in production (observability-cp-canary) for 48h; we measured panics, error rates, metrics fidelity.
- Fall-through behavior: if compact index misses, exporter falls back to storing full logs and issues a high-priority telemetry counter so we can monitor regressions.

Why this is different from previous approaches: Prior sampling was either uniform or strictly cost-thresholded and operated independently of token-phase. By interleaving phases and combining with a lightweight compact index we keep queryable fidelity where teams care (start tokens, finalization) while removing repeated steady-state noise with a low-cost index reference model.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for sampler logic and indexer dedupe
- [x] Integration tests against local exporter + backend emulator
- [x] Benchmarks and measurement harness added to perf/benchmarks/streaming-compact
- [x] Dashboard panels and runbook snippets included
- [x] Feature flag and per-tenant opt-in implemented

Merge decision: Squashed and merged after 2 approvals and green CI. Canary metrics passed acceptance criteria and SLO signal preserved for monitored routes.

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on interleaved_sampler.go policy transitions and the compact index shard eviction heuristics. The index format is intentionally minimal to allow backfill and incremental rollouts.

testing_summary: Unit tests: 98% coverage across sampler and indexer modules. Integration: emulator-based tests simulate 10k concurrent streams and verify dedupe+backfill flow. Perf: benchmark harness shows 3-8% CPU overhead in exporter for canary workload, offset by 40-60% savings in storage and query CPU for heavy stream routes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary (observability-cp-canary) 5% traffic, 48h. Phase 2: tenant opt-in via Console toggle and Dedicated per-tenant config. Phase 3: automatic opt-in for new tenants after 90 days if no regressions. Emergency kill switch: feature_flag.observability.interleaved_sampler = false and a runtime toggle to force-emit full traces. Rollout notes added to runbook.
notes_for_ops: Watch obs.compact_index_miss > 0.1% sustained and obs.span_sample_rate drift on golden routes. If miss rate spikes, revert canary and raise SUP ticket. Storage reclaim happens asynchronously; expect visible reduction after index compaction job completes (24h window).
